writtenTo: The worshipping community of Israel and all believers
importantNotes: Psalms is the longest book of the Bible with 150 chapters.
Psalm 22 is a detailed messianic prophecy describing crucifixion written 1,000 years before Christ.
Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible — each section celebrates God's Word.
The Psalms were designed to be sung — they are the worship music of ancient Israel.
Jesus quoted the Psalms more than any other Old Testament book.

chapters.1: The blessed life of the righteous vs. the way of the wicked.
chapters.2: A messianic psalm — the Lord's Anointed King will rule the nations.
chapters.3: A psalm of David fleeing Absalom — God is a shield around me.
chapters.4: An evening prayer for peace and trust in the Lord.
chapters.5: A morning prayer for God's guidance and protection from enemies.
chapters.6: A prayer for mercy in distress — one of the penitential psalms.
chapters.7: David appeals to God as righteous judge against his accusers.
chapters.8: The majesty of God displayed in creation; the dignity of humanity.
chapters.9: Praise for God's justice against the wicked nations.
chapters.10: A cry against the wicked who oppress the helpless.
chapters.11: Trust in the LORD when everything seems to collapse.
chapters.12: A prayer against deceitful and flattering speech.
chapters.13: How long, O Lord? A psalm moving from lament to trust.
chapters.14: The fool says in his heart 'There is no God.'
chapters.15: Who may dwell on God's holy mountain? Those who live with integrity.
chapters.16: A psalm of confidence — God is my refuge; my heart is glad.
chapters.17: A prayer for vindication and protection from violent enemies.
chapters.18: David's song of deliverance — the LORD is my rock and fortress.
chapters.19: The heavens declare God's glory; the perfection of God's law.
chapters.20: A prayer for the king's victory in battle.
chapters.21: Thanksgiving for the king's victories given by God.
chapters.22: Messianic psalm of suffering — 'My God, why have you forsaken me?'
chapters.23: The LORD is my shepherd — the most beloved psalm.
chapters.24: The King of Glory enters — who may ascend the hill of the LORD?
chapters.25: A prayer for guidance, forgiveness, and protection.
chapters.26: A psalm of integrity — 'Test me, LORD, and try me.'
chapters.27: The LORD is my light and salvation — whom shall I fear?
chapters.28: A cry for help and a song of praise when prayer is answered.
chapters.29: The voice of the LORD in the storm — powerful and majestic.
chapters.30: Praise for healing — weeping may last for a night, but joy comes in the morning.
chapters.31: A prayer of trust — 'Into your hands I commit my spirit.'
chapters.32: The blessedness of forgiveness — a penitential psalm.
chapters.33: Praise to the Creator and Sustainer of all things.
chapters.34: Taste and see that the LORD is good — praise in all circumstances.
chapters.35: A prayer for God to fight against David's enemies.
chapters.36: The wickedness of the sinful vs. the steadfast love of God.
chapters.37: Do not fret because of evildoers — trust in the LORD and do good.
chapters.38: A penitential psalm — suffering under the weight of sin.
chapters.39: A meditation on the brevity and fragility of life.
chapters.40: Thanksgiving for deliverance; a song of God's faithfulness.
chapters.41: Blessed is the one who considers the poor — a psalm of trust.
chapters.42: As the deer pants for water, so my soul pants for God.
chapters.43: A prayer for God's light and truth to lead the way.
chapters.44: A national lament — God, why have you rejected us?
chapters.45: A royal wedding psalm — the King in all His beauty.
chapters.46: God is our refuge and strength — be still and know that I am God.
chapters.47: God reigns over the nations — clap your hands and shout for joy.
chapters.48: The beauty and security of Zion, the city of God.
chapters.49: Wealth cannot redeem a life — only God can ransom a soul.
chapters.50: God speaks as Judge — He desires thanksgiving, not empty ritual.
chapters.51: David's prayer of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba — 'Create in me a clean heart.'
chapters.52: Judgment on the deceitful; the righteous flourish like an olive tree.
chapters.53: The fool says there is no God — similar to Psalm 14.
chapters.54: A prayer for deliverance when betrayed by those who should help.
chapters.55: A lament over betrayal by a close friend — cast your cares on the LORD.
chapters.56: Trust in God when afraid — 'In God I trust, I will not be afraid.'
chapters.57: A prayer of confidence in the shadow of God's wings.
chapters.58: A psalm calling for justice against corrupt rulers.
chapters.59: A prayer for deliverance from violent enemies.
chapters.60: A national lament after military defeat — a prayer for restoration.
chapters.61: Lead me to the rock that is higher than I — a prayer from the ends of the earth.
chapters.62: My soul finds rest in God alone — wait silently for Him.
chapters.63: A psalm of longing for God in the wilderness — 'My soul thirsts for you.'
chapters.64: A prayer for protection from the plots of the wicked.
chapters.65: Praise to God who provides for the earth with rain and harvest.
chapters.66: Shout for joy — praise for God's awesome deeds and answered prayer.
chapters.67: A prayer for God's blessing so that all nations will praise Him.

chapters.69: A messianic psalm of suffering — 'Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my neck.'
chapters.70: An urgent cry for God's quick help — similar to Psalm 40:13-17.

chapters.72: A prayer for the king — a vision of the Messiah's just and everlasting reign.
chapters.73: Asaph's struggle with the prosperity of the wicked — resolved in God's presence.
chapters.74: A lament over the destruction of the Temple — 'How long, O God?'
chapters.75: God the righteous judge will bring the wicked down at the appointed time.
chapters.76: God is victorious in Zion — His power is terrifying and glorious.
chapters.77: A psalm of doubt and remembrance — recalling God's mighty deeds in the past.
chapters.78: A historical psalm recounting God's faithfulness and Israel's rebellion from Egypt onward.
chapters.79: A lament over the destruction of Jerusalem — a prayer for mercy.
chapters.80: A prayer for restoration — 'Restore us, O God; let your face shine.'

chapters.82: God judges unjust rulers — 'Defend the weak and the fatherless.'
chapters.83: A prayer against a coalition of enemies threatening Israel.
chapters.84: How lovely is your dwelling place, O LORD — a psalm of longing for God's presence.
chapters.85: A prayer for national revival — 'Will you not revive us again?'
chapters.86: A prayer of David — 'Teach me your way, LORD, that I may rely on your faithfulness.'
chapters.87: Zion, the city of God — all nations will find their home there.

chapters.89: God's covenant with David; a lament that God seems to have rejected His anointed.
chapters.90: Moses' prayer — God is eternal; human life is brief. 'Teach us to number our days.'
chapters.91: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest in His shadow — divine protection.
chapters.92: A Sabbath song of praise — the righteous will flourish like a palm tree.
chapters.93: The LORD reigns — He is robed in majesty; the world is firmly established.
chapters.94: A cry for God to bring justice against oppressors of His people.
chapters.95: Come, let us worship and bow down — do not harden your hearts as Israel did.
chapters.96: Sing to the LORD a new song — declare His glory among the nations.
chapters.97: The LORD reigns — rejoice! Righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne.
chapters.98: A new song of praise — the LORD has made His salvation known.
chapters.99: The LORD reigns — He is holy. Exalt the LORD our God.
chapters.100: A psalm of thanksgiving — enter His gates with praise; His love endures forever.
chapters.101: David's psalm of integrity — how a godly leader should live.
chapters.102: A prayer of the afflicted — 'Hear my prayer, O LORD.' God is eternal, even when we suffer.
chapters.103: Praise the LORD, O my soul — He forgives, heals, redeems, and crowns with love.
chapters.104: A magnificent hymn celebrating God as Creator and Sustainer of all life.
chapters.105: A historical psalm praising God's faithfulness from Abraham to the Promised Land.
chapters.106: A historical psalm confessing Israel's repeated failures and God's persistent mercy.
chapters.107: Give thanks to the LORD — He delivers from distress, exile, darkness, and storms.
chapters.108: A song of confidence combining portions of Psalms 57 and 60.
chapters.109: An imprecatory psalm — a prayer for judgment on a malicious accuser.
chapters.110: A messianic psalm — 'The LORD said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand.'
chapters.111: An acrostic psalm praising God's great works and faithfulness.
chapters.112: An acrostic psalm describing the blessings of the righteous person.
chapters.113: Praise the LORD — He raises the poor and lifts the needy.
chapters.114: A celebration of the Exodus — the sea fled, the mountains trembled.
chapters.115: Our God is in heaven; He does whatever pleases Him. Trust in the LORD.
chapters.116: A personal thanksgiving for deliverance from death — 'I love the LORD.'
chapters.117: The shortest psalm and shortest chapter — all nations, praise the LORD!
chapters.118: A thanksgiving psalm — 'The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.'
chapters.119: The longest chapter in the Bible — a celebration of God's Word in 176 verses.
chapters.120: A song of ascents — a cry for deliverance from deceitful people.
chapters.121: I lift my eyes to the mountains — my help comes from the LORD.
chapters.122: A song of joy for going to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
chapters.123: A prayer for mercy — our eyes look to the LORD.
chapters.124: If the LORD had not been on our side — a psalm of grateful deliverance.
chapters.125: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion — unshakeable.
chapters.126: When the LORD restored Zion — those who sow in tears will reap with joy.
chapters.127: Unless the LORD builds the house, the builders labor in vain.
chapters.128: Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD — a psalm of family blessing.
chapters.129: A psalm recounting Israel's past oppression and trusting God for deliverance.
chapters.130: Out of the depths I cry to you, LORD — a psalm of waiting for redemption.
chapters.131: A psalm of humble trust — like a weaned child with its mother.
chapters.132: A prayer remembering David's desire to build God a dwelling place.
chapters.133: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity.

chapters.135: Praise the LORD for His greatness and His mighty works in history.

chapters.137: By the rivers of Babylon — a lament of the exiles longing for Jerusalem.
chapters.138: A psalm of wholehearted thanksgiving and trust in God's purposes.
chapters.139: God's complete knowledge and intimate care — 'I am fearfully and wonderfully made.'
chapters.140: A prayer for protection from violent and deceitful enemies.
chapters.141: A prayer for self-control and protection from the traps of the wicked.
chapters.142: David's prayer from the cave — 'I cry aloud to the LORD.'
chapters.143: A prayer for mercy and guidance — 'Teach me to do your will.'
chapters.144: Praise to God who trains hands for battle and gives victory.
chapters.145: David's psalm of praise — the LORD is gracious, compassionate, and faithful.
chapters.146: Praise the LORD — trust in God, not in human leaders.
